Jibril (peace be upon him) kept saying: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqya for you from everything that harms you, from an envier and an evil eye, and Allah will heal you." It was also said: the grain and the date-stone split forth from the earth, the evidence for which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ [6:95]. The original meaning of the word is splitting.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said concerning this: Allah, Exalted is He, uncovered to the hearts of His chosen servants and cast light into them, so the veil split open and the covering was removed.

﴿From the evil of what He created, and from the evil of the darkness when it settles,﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Barza or one of the Banu Shurayk al-Bazzar related to us, saying: Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b related to us, from al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took my hand and pointed to the moon and said: "O 'A'isha, seek refuge with Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/459.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Kharzad al-Basri related to us in Makka, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: Bakkar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf related to us, from his father, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: it is the star when it rises.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Qurazi, al-Farra', Abu 'Ubayda, Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj said:

It is the night.

Ibn Zayd said: meaning also the Pleiades when they set. He said: Diseases and plagues used to increase when they set and would lift when they rose. [[Zad al-Masir: 8/334.]] The root of ghasaq is darkness and standing still [...] [[Unreadable word.]] when it entered; and it was said: a safety that calmed its darkness. [[As in the manuscript.]]

It was also said: the night was called ghasiq because it is cooler than the day; al-ghasiq is cold, and al-ghasq is coldness. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/256.]]

﴿and from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾ means the sorceresses who blow into the knots of the cord when they perform incantations over them. Al-nafth is like blowing, as one does who performs ruqya. 'Antara said:

"If he recovers, I have not blown upon him; and if he dies, the knots are due to him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/257.]]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit recited: "min sharri al-naffathat" in the measure fa'ilat. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/259.]]

﴿and from the evil of an envier when he envies.﴾ al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Allah gathered the evils in this verse and concluded with envy, to make known that it is the basest of dispositions.
